name: Five Pillars of Islam
description: Learn about the 5 pillars of Islam

questions.question: How many pillars of Islam are there?
questions.explanation: There are 5 pillars of Islam: Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, and Hajj.

questions.question: What is the first pillar of Islam?
questions.explanation: Shahada is the declaration that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger.

questions.question: How many times a day do Muslims pray?
questions.explanation: Muslims pray 5 times a day: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha.

questions.question: What is Zakat?
questions.explanation: Zakat is the obligatory charity that Muslims give to help those in need.

questions.question: During which month do Muslims fast?
questions.explanation: Ramadan is the holy month during which Muslims fast from dawn to sunset.

questions.question: What is the pilgrimage to Mecca called?
questions.explanation: Hajj is the annual pilgrimage to Mecca that every able Muslim should perform at least once.

questions.question: Which prayer is performed before sunrise?
questions.explanation: Fajr is the dawn prayer performed before sunrise.

questions.question: What do Muslims do during Sawm (fasting)?
options: Not eat or drink from dawn to sunset
questions.explanation: During Sawm, Muslims abstain from food and drink from dawn until sunset.

questions.question: What percentage of savings should be given as Zakat?
questions.explanation: Muslims give 2.5% of their savings as Zakat each year.

questions.question: What is the meaning of Shahada?
questions.explanation: Shahada is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger.

questions.question: Which prayer is performed at noon?
questions.explanation: Dhuhr is the noon prayer performed when the sun starts to decline.

questions.question: When is the last day of Hajj?
questions.explanation: Hajj ends on the 12th of Dhul Hijjah.

questions.question: What is the Shahada?
questions.explanation: The Shahada is the declaration that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger.

questions.question: Which pillar of Islam is about giving money to help the poor?
questions.explanation: Zakat is the pillar of giving a share of our wealth to those in need.

questions.question: Which building do Muslims face when they pray?
questions.explanation: Muslims all over the world face the Kaaba in Mecca when they pray.

questions.question: What is the call to prayer called?
questions.explanation: The Adhan is the call to prayer announced before each of the five daily prayers.

questions.question: What do Muslims do to get clean before praying?
questions.explanation: Wudu is the special washing Muslims perform before prayer.

questions.question: What is the early morning meal before fasting called?
questions.explanation: Suhoor is the meal eaten before dawn when fasting in Ramadan.

questions.question: What is the meal that breaks the fast at sunset called?
questions.explanation: Iftar is the meal Muslims eat at sunset to end their fast.

questions.question: Which pillar of Islam is a special journey to Mecca?
questions.explanation: Hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims make once in their lifetime if they are able.

questions.question: On which day do Muslims gather for a special weekly prayer?
questions.explanation: Muslims gather every Friday for the Jumu'ah prayer at the mosque.

questions.question: Which prayer do Muslims pray at sunset?
questions.explanation: Maghrib is the prayer performed just after the sun sets.

questions.question: How many rakats (units) are in the Fajr prayer?
questions.explanation: Fajr has 2 rakats and is prayed before sunrise.

questions.question: How many rakats are in the Maghrib prayer?
questions.explanation: Maghrib, the sunset prayer, has 3 rakats.

questions.question: What is the direction of prayer called?
questions.explanation: The Qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face in prayer.

questions.question: What is the person who calls the Adhan called?
questions.explanation: The muezzin is the person who calls the Adhan to announce prayer time.

questions.question: How much of their yearly savings do Muslims usually give as Zakat?
questions.explanation: Muslims give 2.5% of their saved wealth each year as Zakat.

questions.question: In which Islamic month does Hajj take place?
questions.explanation: Hajj takes place in Dhul Hijjah, the last month of the Islamic calendar.

questions.question: What are the two Eid festivals called?
questions.explanation: Muslims celebrate Eid al-Fitr after Ramadan and Eid al-Adha during Hajj season.

questions.question: What are the special night prayers during Ramadan called?
questions.explanation: Taraweeh prayers are extra prayers performed at night during Ramadan.

questions.question: What is the Friday congregational prayer called?
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah is the Friday prayer that replaces Dhuhr and includes a sermon (khutbah).

questions.question: The Shahada says: there is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His ___
questions.explanation: The Shahada declares that Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: How many rakats is the fard (obligatory) part of the Isha prayer?
questions.explanation: The fard part of Isha is 4 rakats.

questions.question: How many fard rakats do Muslims pray in total each day?
questions.explanation: The five daily prayers have 17 fard rakats in total: 2 + 4 + 4 + 3 + 4.

questions.question: Standing on the plain of Arafah is an important part of which pillar?
questions.explanation: Standing at Arafah on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah is one of the most important parts of Hajj.

questions.question: What is walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah called?
questions.explanation: Sa'i is walking seven times between Safa and Marwah, remembering Hajar's search for water.

questions.question: What is circling the Kaaba seven times called?
questions.explanation: Tawaf is circling the Kaaba seven times during Hajj or Umrah.

questions.question: What is the special white clothing worn by pilgrims during Hajj called?
questions.explanation: Ihram is the simple white clothing pilgrims wear, showing everyone is equal before Allah.

questions.question: What is the minimum amount of wealth a Muslim must have before Zakat is due?
questions.explanation: Nisab is the minimum amount of wealth someone must own before they must pay Zakat.

questions.question: What special charity is given at the end of Ramadan before Eid prayer?
questions.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid prayer so everyone can enjoy Eid.

questions.question: Which group of people is NOT required to fast in Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Young children are not required to fast; fasting becomes a duty when a person matures.

questions.question: What is the shorter pilgrimage to Mecca that can be done any time of year?
questions.explanation: Umrah is the shorter pilgrimage that can be performed at any time of the year.
